title: Chanamel the Egyptian
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Chanamel the Egyptian. (Biblical namesake: Chanamel, son of Jeremiah’s uncle Shallum—Jeremiah 32:7.) He was High Priest during the Second Temple period. In his time a red heifer was prepared, as stated in Mishnah Parah 3:4.

Hyman reports from Antiquities of the Jews concerning him that when Herod sat upon his royal throne he raised Chananel, who was from Babylonia, to the High Priesthood, and afterward, at the request of his wife Miriam, removed him for a time; and about him there is extensive discussion in the valuable book Dorot HaRishonim, vol. 1, p. 59b.

notes.text: The Biblical parenthesis is a namesake reference, not an identification of the Second Temple High Priest with Jeremiah’s contemporary. Jeremiah 32:8 calls Chanamel the uncle’s son: Shallum is the uncle. Chanamel and Chananel are retained as printed.

The consulted Mishnah Parah locates Chanamel the Egyptian’s red-heifer notice at 3:5; Hyman’s supplied 3:4 is retained. The Jeremiah parallel concerns a Biblical namesake. Hyman’s Antiquities and Dorot HaRishonim account is reported here without a new historical identification.
